_comment: How the game turns the map data in data/city/ into a town. Coordinates are never typed here: places are named by the streets that meet there, and the game looks them up in the OSM data.

map.name: Sand Bar
map._comment: Which map this is. Trans-Canada Auto is meant to grow a map at a time (one config like this per map); Sand Bar is the first.

origin._comment: World (0,0,0). This is the OSM position of the Great George Street / Richmond Street junction (node 8598664). Keep it fixed when the map grows so existing coordinates stay valid.

play_area._comment: The playable area: the bypass ring (Riverside Drive, the Arterial Highway, Upton Road), closed by the North River and the harbour. 'ring' goes round the edge in order: 'streets' is a junction named by two streets that meet there, and between two such junctions the edge follows the shortest way along the streets in 'follow' ("" lets it through the unnamed roundabouts on Riverside Drive). 'water' is a point out in the river or harbour as [latitude, longitude], the one place coordinates are typed, since water has no street names. The invisible wall sits margin_m outside this line, with road-closed barriers wherever a street crosses it.

ring._comment: the North River, where the Trans-Canada crosses to Cornwall
the Hillsborough River, past the bridge

spawn._comment: Where everyone starts: the lot of the old Blaze Pizza on the north-east corner of University Avenue and Belvedere Avenue (OSM way 1269125411), now the Trans-Canada Auto Visitor Centre. 'pos' is [longitude, latitude] and 'direction' the compass heading you face, as the map editor writes them. Instead of 'pos': 'parkade' (its OSM id, a landmark with style parkade) puts you in its aisle on 'level' (0 is the ground floor), in front of 'stall' (counting from the far end) on 'side' (1 or -1 of the ramp); with neither, on the sidewalk at the junction of 'streets', facing the 'face_toward' junction. The map editor's start (data/edits.json) and a home you own come first.

parked_cars._comment: The one car you start with, cheap on purpose (the Filly, the cheapest car for sale): backed in against the front of the Trans-Canada Auto Visitor Centre, facing out over the lot. 'pos' is [longitude, latitude] and 'direction' the compass heading the car faces. Instead of 'pos': in a parkade, backed into 'stall' on 'level' and 'side' (as for the spawn); otherwise against the right-hand curb, on 'street', 'distance_m' from the junction with 'from', heading toward 'toward'. 'model' is an id in scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd; 'colour' is a hex colour or the model's first colour if left out.

work_yard._comment: The truck yard: Delayed & Lost Trucking's, in the McQuaid's Moving and Storage lot off Riverside Drive (OSM way 297177033); its dispatch window, Surplus counter and lending bays are in scripts/economy/delayed_lost.gd. Its lidar trees stand in islands; everything here sits in the drive aisles between them, clear of the trunks. 'pos' (longitude, latitude) is the middle of the lot and 'direction' the compass heading its long side runs, the same as a map editor spot. Each vehicle and load is placed by 'at': metres [right, back] from the middle, facing 'direction' turned by 'heading' degrees clockwise; 'lift' raises a load (1.52 puts it on a flatbed trailer's deck). Vehicle 'model' ids are in scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd and truck_models.gd; load 'kind's are in scripts/vehicles/cargo.gd.

fleet_cars._comment: Fleet cars, always where they are here even when the map editor places the other cars: model (scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd), livery (CarModels.LIVERIES), unit (the number on the plate and sides), pos [longitude, latitude] and direction (compass degrees the nose points). The Charlatown Police Services squad cars, nosed in along the station's south-east wall on Kirkwood Drive (Joe's note: Dodge Journeys and some Dodge Rams; ours are Dodgy Jaunts and Rammers).

road_defaults._comment: By OSM highway class: curb-to-curb width (two-way and one-way), sidewalk width, and for highways the paved shoulder outside the edge line. When OSM gives a lane count the width is lanes x lane + both shoulders. A class with a shoulder is built highway style: no curbs or sidewalks, white edge lines, gravel verges.

minor_roads._comment: Roads outside drivable_classes that are still built, plain asphalt with no curbs, sidewalks or paint (see road_defaults): OSM service roads whose service= value is listed here ('' is a service road with none: the lanes through a campus, a hospital, a lot or an industrial park, like Lily Pond Drive and the Ravenwood Drives), and tracks with a name (Wharf Road, Ferry Road). Driveways, parking aisles and drive-throughs stay painted on the ground. Pieces underground (layer below 0) are left out.

street_overrides._comment: Widths measured against OSM building footprints (median gap between building fronts across each street, inside the play area). Curb + sidewalk must stay inside that gap.

brick_streets._comment: Victoria Row: the brick block of Richmond Street between Queen and Great George.

neighbourhoods._comment: Each neighbourhood's own look for its ordinary houses and apartment blocks (outside downtown; landmarks, brands and churches keep theirs): centre [latitude, longitude] and radius_m (the nearest centre whose radius reaches a building wins), and houses / apartments, each with styles (weights by style name: clapboard, shingle, brick, painted, modern), colours (siding), roof_colours (pitched roofs) and trim. From local news and listings, best judgment where nobody wrote about it. yards: what stands in its houses' yards (see "yards").

What stands in ordinary houses' yards (scripts/world/town_dressing.gd): a profile for each neighbourhood (its "yards" in "neighbourhoods"), "downtown" (inside heritage_district_m) and "default" for the rest. front: weights of what's on the front lot line (none, hedge, picket_fence, chain_link, split_rail, stone_wall, wood_fence), with gaps for the walk and the driveway; back: what's round the back yard (back_height sets its height); shed, trampoline, fire_pit (with two lawn chairs), picnic_table: the share of houses with one; carts: the share with the Waste Watch cart out at the end of the driveway: black with blue recycling bags one week, green compost the next, the week picked per street (there is no blue cart on PEI); mailbox_post: the share with a mailbox on a post at the road, on streets with no sidewalk. pedestrian_malls._comment: Streets closed to cars and given over to patios in season: no cars parked along them (StreetProps._curb_parking), on the named street within radius_m of at [latitude, longitude]. Victoria Row is Richmond Street from Queen to Great George, closed May to October (CBC).

landmarks._comment: Extra detail for well-known buildings, matched by OSM way id. Footprints still come from OSM; these set what the footprint can't tell us. Colours, heights and towers are best estimates, not measurements. Entries can be small: one that only sets colours or materials keeps the building's measured lidar height and roof (set wall_height or roof to override those). Keys: style (brick, clapboard, sandstone, painted, modern, shingle, church), colour, roof_colour, spire_colour, wall_height (m), roof (flat, gabled or hipped), pitch (degrees), chimneys (how many, in pairs along the ridge of a pitched roof), trim (white, cream, green, black), shop, awning (a colour, or none), sign (a name board over the front), cornice (false for a plain top), towers (front_pair, front_center, front_corner), tower_size, tower_height, spire_height, tower_protrude (m), portico, portico_width, ribbed (ribbed sandstone with slot windows), massing ("confederation" for its extra blocks), and where the front is: front_toward [street, street] (faces that junction), front_toward_spot [latitude, longitude] (faces that spot, e.g. where a field note was taken) or front_street; front_line: main runs the front along the main wall the whole width of the building, past vestibules standing out of it. Big stores and plazas: roof mansard (a sloping skirt of shingles round a flat top) with eave_height, roof_top and roof_overhang (m out from the walls, a covered walk on posts when over 1 m), shopfront: front (shop glass on the front wall only), style: tank (a white storage tank with a stair up its side; roof cone or dome, dome_width, sign and logo for an oil company's name between chevrons), and entrances, a list of tall glass A-frames through the roof, each {at (0 to 1 along the front from its left end as you face it), width, depth, ridge, sign, sign_colour, sign_text}; one without a sign shows the brand's name. An entrance or wall sign with spot [latitude, longitude] and facing stands on the wall nearest that spot that looks that way, centred where the spot meets it (a mall's doors and stores on every side). facades: a list of units (as in units, with spot, facing and width instead of from and to), each standing on the wall nearest its spot: a mall's storefronts and cladding on any side. A unit's top_colour and top_height put a band of a second colour across its top (a metal fascia over stucco). An entrance with shape: tower is a flat-topped glass tower instead (Princess Auto's): height, cap, cap_colour, doors (height of the shop doors), band {colour, text, text_colour, reach} a canopy over the doors with text on its edge, accent {colour, width, side} a strip of colour on the wall beside it. wall_signs: a list of names or logos on walls other than the front, each {facing (compass degrees the wall looks toward), at (0 to 1 along it from its left end as you face it), sign, sign_colour ("wall" for letters straight on the wall), sign_text, sign_height, sign_y}. base_colour and base_height put a base course along the front of a store with entrances; windows: false leaves the walls blank. Quick oil changes built the Pro Oil way: barrel {height, radius} (a round tower like an oil drum, the way in, with the name on it; it stands on the footprint's round part, or the front's right-hand corner) and bay_doors (drive-through bays, a door at each end down both long sides). Strip plazas: units, the shops along the front left to right, each {from, to (0 to 1 along the front from its left end as you face it), colour (its facade over the shop glass), height (a raised parapet over the roof, m), glass (false for a blank wall), band (a dark canopy fascia over the glass), sign, sign_colour (the board, else the facade's colour), sign_text, sign_height}; each stands on the footprint's own front wall where it is; front_depth (m, default 6) is how far back from the front line walls still get shop glass. Any building: base_colour and base_height (a brick base course round the walls), cap_colour and cap_height (a band of colour along the top edge). doors: a list of overhead doors on a wall, each {facing (compass degrees the wall looks toward), count, from, to (0 to 1 along the wall from its left end as you face it), width, height, sill (m: 1.2 makes them loading docks with rubber bumpers), colour, frame, windows (a row of glass across each)}. A building drawn in the map editor (data/edits.json) takes a landmark entry by its id, like "edit:dl_office". Quick oil changes built the Pro Oil way: barrel {height, radius} (a round tower like an oil drum, the way in, with the name on it; it stands on the footprint's round part, or the front's right-hand corner) and bay_doors (drive-through bays, a door at each end down both long sides).

Federal research station on the 35-ha experimental farm (est. 1909) between Belvedere Avenue and Allen Street. Ottawa declared the land surplus in 2002, then changed its mind. Dec 2023: the mayor floated housing on the farm; Coun. Tweel opposed. Fields, ponds, community gardens and the Confederation Trail behind. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-experimental-farm-1.7056202, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-tweel-experimental-farm-development-1.7064812

28331503.name: CBC P.E.I. building, 430 University Avenue
28331503._comment: From CBC's photos: Low 1960s/70s complex, one storey plus a two-storey studio block. Walls buff/tan brick under a deep dark-brown metal fascia; a newer wing in dark charcoal metal siding with a row of windows; a taller two-storey brick block with a pale metal-panel top behind. Entrance (since 2019) under a bright red box canopy with 'CBC Radio-Canada' and the gem logo in white, number 430 on the brown fascia, steps and a ramp with metal railings. A tall white pylon sign with the red gem on the lawn by University Avenue. A red-and-white lattice radio mast and satellite dishes behind. CBC's Charlottetown radio and TV station. In 2018 CBC chose a $2M renovation over a new building; work delayed (2019, then COVID); new glassed-in radio studio by the front door opened July 2020 so people outside can see in. The old studio is a windowless brick bunker in the core. Joe's photo should correct it. 220517591.name: Holy Redeemer Church (Roman Catholic), 3 Pond Street
220517591._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Interior photos: 1960s modern, walls of warm brown brick, sloping wood-lined ceiling, tall narrow coloured-glass slot windows. Exterior (guess from the date and inside): a broad low brown-brick church with a shallow gabled roof of dark shingles or metal, tall slot windows down the sides, a plain bell tower or tall cross at the front, glass entrance doors under a flat canopy facing Pond Street, big parking lot. The Jack Blanchard Family Centre and other parish buildings stand beside it. Parish founded 1929 by the Redemptorists (who left in 1975); the present church complex was built in 1964. One of the city's biggest Catholic churches: Christmas Eve masses for up to 1,300. Hosts the annual Police and Peace Officers' Memorial Service (Sept 2023 photos inside). Graffiti spray-painted on it (2000s). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-police-memorial-charlottetown-1.6977069, https://redemptorists.ca/archives/prince-edward-island (search snippet)

28433871.name: Kiwanis Dairy Bar, Victoria Park (by the boardwalk)
28433871._comment: From CBC's photos: Small one-storey stand, bright yellow clapboard with white trim and white corner boards, a front-gabled roof of grey shingles carried forward over a deep open porch on yellow turned posts; serving windows under the porch with white shutters. An oval sign on the gable: an ice-cream cone with 'Kiwanis Dairy Bar, Since 1955' in navy on white. Grey wooden deck with board railing, red-painted metal railing, picnic tables on the grass looking at the harbour. Run by the Kiwanis Club since 1955; P.E.I.'s oldest operating dairy bar. One operator for over four decades. March 2024 asked the city for $50K toward a $600K expansion (walk-in freezer, storage, staff washroom). Renovated: grand reopening and 70th birthday July 19, 2025 with 70-cent ice cream; first major update since the 1990s. About 22 hard-serve flavours plus soft serve. Proceeds go to children's charities. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/kiwanis-dairy-expansion-1.7152822, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-kiwanis-dairy-bar-70th-birthday-1.7589398, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-ice-cream-dairy-bars-history-1.6547533

28433895.name: Aubin-Arsenault Building (provincial offices), behind Government House
28433895._comment: From CBC's photos: Three-storey long office block, flat roof, pale greyish-lilac/beige siding or panel with white trim and regular windows, a small pedimented entrance bay with a porch roof at its east end. Parking beside it. Provincial government office building just north of Government House, at the Brighton edge of Victoria Park. Joe's photo should correct it.

28331894.name: Government House (Fanningbank), 1 Terry Fox Drive, Victoria Park
28331894._comment: From CBC's photos: Large white two-storey wooden house, shutters dark green, low hipped roof of grey shingles with four tall red-brick chimneys. Centre front (south, toward the harbour) a two-storey portico of white columns under a pediment, and a one-storey veranda on white columns wrapping the front and sides. Lower white wings at the back. Gravel drive loops to the front; a formal hedged garden (box hedges, roses, peonies) east of the house. Lieutenant-governor's residence, built 1834 (designer Isaac Smith), wood frame, Georgian/Palladian; land set aside by Governor Fanning (1789). In 1873 16 ha of its farm became Victoria Park. National Historic Site. Gardens reopened to the public 2021. A 2015 NDP proposal to make it a museum went nowhere. The LG's office costs taxpayers about $650K a year (2015 article). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/government-house-book-1.3418508, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-fanningbank-lieutenant-governor-perry-garden-1.6080325, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/ndp-leader-wants-to-turn-fanningbank-into-museum-1.2899206

221633605.name: Spring Park Elementary School, 30 Dunkirk Street
221633605._comment: From CBC's photos: Modern two-storey school. The gym block is red brick on its lower part and dark royal-blue ribbed metal above, the blue cut along its bottom edge into a row of house-shaped (pointed gable) notches over the brick; 'SPRING PARK SCHOOL' in white serif letters on the brick corner. Long low classroom wings of grey/white metal panel and light brick with ribbon windows, some yellow accent panels. Entrance under a flat navy-blue box canopy on posts. Front faces Dunkirk Street (west) across a lot; flagpole with the Canadian flag beside the gym. New school opened 2013 and overcrowded almost from day one: 24 classrooms for 29 homerooms (2018); rezoning of some students to West Royalty Elementary phased in over five years (2019). Oct 2024 the custodians' union said students in some Island schools were being taught in closets and under staircases, Spring Park named. A buddy bench was installed (2016). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-public-schools-branch-spring-park-elementary-1.7339736, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-public-schools-branch-review-recommendations-rezoning-1.4943868, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-spring-park-school-first-day-1.4278588

28344786.name: Queen Charlotte Intermediate School, 150 North River Road
28344786._comment: From CBC's photos: Mid-century red brick, two storeys. The main classroom wing has long window bands with green ribbed-metal panels between the floors; a taller plain brick gym/auditorium block faces North River Road with 'QUEEN CHARLOTTE INTERMEDIATE' in white letters under a thin green metal cap and over a flat entrance canopy. 'MAIN ENTRANCE' on a small gold plaque over glass doors reached by yellow-painted concrete steps. Front faces North River Road (west), with parking along the road. Grades 7-9, about 650 students, over capacity. Nov 2023 the province committed almost $17M over four years for about 10,000 sq ft more space plus new windows, floors and lighting; a later capital plan says $21M. Roof damaged by Fiona (Sept 2022). Sits beside Simmons and Colonel Gray; the new turf field is next to it. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-queen-charlotte-school-getting-17m-deal-with-overcapacity-1.7016082, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-queen-charlotte-intermediate-diversity-flags-1.6054040

r6565581.name: Colonel Gray Senior High School, 175 Spring Park Road
r6565581._comment: From CBC's photos: Long 1960s/70s school, two and three storeys, flat roofs (dark brown/black membrane in the aerial). Red-brown brick walls with long horizontal bands of windows separated by white/light-grey panel spandrels. Main entrance: a row of grey-framed glass double doors under a wide light-grey concrete/panel band carrying 'COLONEL GRAY SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL' in raised dark-grey capitals. Front faces Spring Park Road (east); a long walk across the front lawn to the doors; a flagpole on the lawn. Senior high (grades 10-12). Simmons rebuilt right beside it (its footprint moved closer to the school). June 2024 Charlottetown police tactical unit staged a mock lockdown there for training. Rezoning (2025-26): Queen Charlotte Intermediate students now feed into Colonel Gray; Stratford's new high school opening next fall moves hundreds of students. 2019 vaping crackdown; 2017 the school removed pop. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-colonel-gray-cracking-down-on-vaping-1.5347386, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-2020-grad-signs-colonel-gray-high-school-1.5600307, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-police-training-scenario-1.7248538

28344793.name: Simmons Sports Centre (new, opened Dec 2, 2024), North River Road
28344793._comment: From CBC's photos: A tall white box for the rink: white ribbed metal walls with thin dark-grey vertical slot windows in irregular groups, a low-slope light-grey metal roof with a block of solar panels at the north-east end. A lower one/two-storey front block (lobby, change rooms) at its south-west end: flat white roof, walls of grey metal panel with a long band of warm wood (cedar-look) cladding and glass, a glassed atrium entrance under a wood-slat soffit. Inside the doors 'SIMMONS Sports Centre' in silver letters on barnboard wood. The outdoor pool sits in a fenced concrete deck beside the low block (aerial photo: on its south-west side toward the parking lot), with lane ropes, umbrellas and loungers. Parking lot on the west side toward North River Road; Colonel Gray's brown roofs just east; playing fields and the new turf field to the north. Replaces the 50-year-old Simmons arena and its 50-year-old outdoor pool. Council approved plans Jan 2022; budget rose from about $25M to $33M (Nov 2023) and came in about $36M. Due to open Oct 14, 2024; a leak in the 18 km of pipe under the ice slab delayed it to Dec 2, 2024 (repairs under warranty). The old arena beside it was demolished in 2024 (some funding was tied to knocking it down before the new one worked). NHL-sized rink seating about 600, six dressing rooms, two-lane walking track upstairs, multi-purpose room. Outdoor six-lane 25 m pool opened June 22, 2025; in Sept 2026 a survey found it 8 to 12 mm too short for Swimming Canada certification, and the builder started fixing it Sept 11, 2026. A $250K naming-rights offer was withdrawn. OSM's footprint has no lidar height, so it is the new building (the 2020 lidar saw the old one). base band stands in for the wood-clad lobby block; the rink box is 12 to 13 m Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-new-simmons-sports-centre-opening-charlottetown-1.7398462, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-simmons-sport-centre-update-1.7029272, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-simmons-pool-short-competition-9.7318544

The Irving-owned (JD Irving) chain's Charlottetown store on Walsh Road (it used to be on Allen Street). Fire in the store in 2015 (electrical suspected). An injured coyote took refuge in the yard by the ice-melt pallets in Nov 2022. Open holidays, pet-friendly. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/fire-strikes-kent-building-supplies-in-charlottetown-1.3139396, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-coyote-kent-building-supplies-1.6730095

390223206.name: Nursing-home wing by Hunt Avenue (unnamed)
390223206._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): As 390223205. As 390223205. Joe's photo should correct it.

390223205.name: Nursing-home wing by Hunt Avenue (unnamed)
390223205._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): One-storey, beige siding, hipped grey roof. OSM nursing_home beside Charlotte Court / Garden Home. Joe's photo should correct it.

390223204.name: Charlotte Court seniors' apartments, 300 North River Road
390223204._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess from the date: three-storey apartment wings (13 m), vinyl siding in beige/light grey with white trim and a brick or stone base, gabled roofs of grey shingles with small front gables over the entrances, patios/balconies. Provincial seniors' social housing; 48 affordable apartments (12 barrier-free) built by Killam/APM, opened 2011, replacing the original Charlotte Court (the oldest of its kind on PEI, then demolished). Private patios; fitness room, card room, BBQ area. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://cmhc-schl.gc.ca/professionals/industry-innovation-and-leadership/industry-expertise/affordable-housing/case-studies-and-testimonials/charlotte-court-charlottetown-prince-edward-island (search snippet), https://archivenews.princeedwardisland.ca/charlotte-court-redevelopment-project-nears-completion (search snippet)

390223203.name: Charlotte Court seniors' apartments, 300 North River Road
390223203._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess from the date: three-storey apartment wings (13 m), vinyl siding in beige/light grey with white trim and a brick or stone base, gabled roofs of grey shingles with small front gables over the entrances, patios/balconies. Provincial seniors' social housing; 48 affordable apartments (12 barrier-free) built by Killam/APM, opened 2011, replacing the original Charlotte Court (the oldest of its kind on PEI, then demolished). Private patios; fitness room, card room, BBQ area. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://cmhc-schl.gc.ca/professionals/industry-innovation-and-leadership/industry-expertise/affordable-housing/case-studies-and-testimonials/charlotte-court-charlottetown-prince-edward-island (search snippet), https://archivenews.princeedwardisland.ca/charlotte-court-redevelopment-project-nears-completion (search snippet)

388750694.name: The Garden Home (long-term care), 310 North River Road
388750694._comment: From CBC's photos: Sprawling one-storey care home: white stucco/siding walls on a red-brick base, a mansard-like roof of weathered brown-grey cedar shakes all round, front gables with Tudor-style dark half-timbering, a gabled entrance porch on white posts. A dark-green sign with gold letters 'ENHANCED LIVING CENTRES / GARDEN HOME' between two red-brick piers on the lawn by North River Road, a flagpole with the PEI flag, clipped shrubs, benches with red slats along the walks, white railings. Private nursing home run by P.E.I. Seniors Homes / Enhanced Living Centres. On a provisional licence since Jan 2022 (needed improvements to meet standards). Opened an 11-bed secure dementia unit May 2021 by converting existing beds. Three new beds approved in 2024. Had six centenarians at once in 2018. (Not in this area's list but the brief names it.) Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-dementia-garden-home-health-pei-1.6006813, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-long-term-care-provisional-license-1.6734439, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-centenarians-the-garden-home-words-of-wisdom-1.4574099

1075433239.name: Centennial used cars and car wash
1075433239._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): One-storey, white panels, two wash bays with roll-up doors. Used-car office and car wash beside the Nissan dealer. Joe's photo should correct it.

701204254.name: Centennial Nissan, 2 Upton Road -> proposed 'Bicentennial Nissun'
701204254._comment: From CBC's photos: From the photo's corner: Nissan's dealer look: a pylon with a red-framed white sign and the chrome Nissan logo ring; the building likely white and silver composite panels (#e6e7e8) with a dark grey entrance portal and big showroom glass, flat roof, service bays at the back. Dealer at 2 Upton Road at the Maypoint roundabout (also listed at 30 Nicholas Lane); its sign shows in a CBC Capital Drive detour photo (2020). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.carpages.ca/dealer/charlottetown/centennial-nissan-of-charlottetown/credit (snippet), https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-capital-drive-detour-1.5820660

845193220.name: Ultramar canopy -> Ultrasea
845193220._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Flat white canopy with a blue fascia and red stripe on steel posts. Fuel canopy (see the store). Joe's photo should correct it.

845193219.name: Ultramar store and car wash, Capital Drive at Maypoint Road -> Ultrasea
845193219._comment: From news and listings (no photo): A 2018-era station store: one storey, light grey/white panels (#e4e4e0) with a blue fascia band (#1f3f8f), a red stripe, glass front facing the pumps. Parkland Fuel applied to IRAC in Oct 2017 for an Ultramar, convenience store, stand-alone car wash and maybe a restaurant at the southeast corner of Capital Drive and Maypoint Road; DP Murphy (building the Hampton) supported it as the 'gateway to the city'. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.4371339

450238221.name: Maypoint Plaza, Maypoint Road at Capital Drive
450238221._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): One-storey strip, beige stucco/siding (#d6ccb8), dark fascia band, four or five units with glass fronts toward its lot. Small plaza at the Maypoint roundabout (a vacation listing calls it 'near Maypoint Plaza'); tenants unknown. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.expedia.nl/Charlottetown-Hotels-Maypoint-Vacation-Home.h127176618.Hotelinfo (snippet)

450238222.name: Former RCMP Queens District detachment, 153 Maypoint Road (closed 2025)
450238222._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a 1990s one-storey office of tan brick (#b8946c) with a hipped dark roof, a fenced compound with a garage at the back, now empty: the crest and letters gone from the wall (ghost outline), a FOR LEASE sign. Queens District RCMP were here 20-plus years (since the 1990s; 'more than 30 years in Queens County'). Closed to the public May 5, 2025; moved to a new ~$25M, 23,626 sq ft detachment on Mercedes Drive in Cornwall, opened Aug 2025 (a year late; first estimate $18.5M). The chief superintendent called Maypoint 'not a functional detachment': cramped, no cells, no space to process prisoners. 153 Maypoint Road showed up in a commercial real-estate listing (search snippet). The RCMP firearms office is listed at 161 Maypoint Road. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-rcmp-cornwall-new-digs-1.7615950, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-rcmp-queens-district-new-detachment-cornwall-1.7526137, https://richardrutkowski.evrealestate.com/listing-detail/1164554219/153_Maypoint_Road-Charlottetown (snippet)

385049904.name: Irish Cultural Centre (Benevolent Irish Society hall), 582 North River Road
385049904._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a small one-storey hall, white or green vinyl/clapboard siding (#e9e6dc) with green trim (#2e6b3a), a gabled roof, a gabled entry porch, a shamrock sign; the Irish tricolour and Canadian flag out front. The Benevolent Irish Society (founded 1825) hall: lectures (series 30 years old in 2017), ceilidhs, step-dancing, St. Patrick's variety show, Christmas tea and craft fair, its New Year's levee since the '80s; an Irish/Celtic library opened 2019 (room for 4,000-5,000 books). The building is named for a 19th-century politician: leave the name off the sign. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-irish-library-benevolent-society-1.5066431, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-st-patricks-day-irish-fitzgerald-benevolent-1.4577479, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-2021-levee-day-tribute-1.5858444

390220216.name: West Royalty Community Centre
390220216._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a one-storey 1970s-80s hall with a taller gym block, walls of beige vinyl siding or tan brick (#cbbfa6) and brown trim, a low-pitched or flat roof, glass doors under a small canopy, City of Charlottetown sign. City-owned community centre by Lower Malpeque Road and Kirkdale Road: a gym (youth committee wanted free gym hours), meeting room for ~200 (the 2019 asphalt-plant meeting), singles club Mondays, Jingle Bell Walk, mural sessions in 2017, a device-charging centre after Hurricane Dorian (2019), gender-neutral washrooms planned 2020. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-sociable-singles-aug-2019-1.5262853, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-asphalt-plant-residents-1.5207733, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-hurricane-dorian-sunday-sept-2019-1.5275152

178056200.name: Beach Grove Home, 200 Beach Grove Road
178056200._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a 1980s one-storey care home, long wings, walls of brown/red brick base with beige siding (#d2c6b0), dark brown trim, low hipped or gabled roofs in brown/grey shingle (#5a4f48), a covered entrance. Public long-term care home: 130 beds in three households (Meadow, Harbour, Sunset; Harbour has a bilingual francophone neighbourhood since 2019), three respite beds. 30th anniversary in 2016 (opened 1986). A COVID outbreak in Meadow in Feb 2023. The 3.5 km Beach Grove trail runs round the property with harbour views. The province owns the land around it, 'surrounded by government buildings', and planned 30 seniors' apartments next door (2021). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/en/information/health-pei/beach-grove-home (snippet), https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-beach-grove-seniors-housing-1.6135602, https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.3592638

450616448.name: Prince Edward Home, 75 Maypoint Road
450616448._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a long, low one- and two-storey home in 'households' wings off a central entrance, walls of tan/beige brick base with light vinyl or fibre-cement siding above (#d8cfbf), lots of windows, a canopy over the entrance, hipped dark grey shingle roofs (#53565a). Public long-term care home run by Health PEI: 120 beds, private rooms, two respite beds, dementia care. The replacement for the old Prince Edward Home downtown (plans from ~2008), built in the 2010s by Maypoint Road. Health PEI added temporary beds here in 2026 to ease hospital pressure. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://qatauth.gpei.ca/en/node/59221 (snippet: 120 beds, 75 Maypoint Road), https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/p-e-i-plans-replacements-for-long-term-care-homes-1.707534, https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/9.7136743

543734321.name: Grace Baptist Church, 50 Kirkdale Road
543734321._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Guess: a 1990s-2000s suburban church: tan/beige brick or vinyl (#cdbfa6), a large low-pitched gabled sanctuary roof in dark grey (#4f5357), a gabled glass entry with a modest white steeple or cross, a flat-roofed hall wing. Baptist church at 50 Kirkdale Road, West Royalty (search snippets); north of Capital Drive opposite the Holiday Inn Express (CBC's map). Big footprint (2,398 m2): a church with a gym/hall wing. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://atlanticcanada.thegospelcoalition.org/atlantic-canada-churches/church/1/grace-baptist-church-prince-edward-island (snippet)

400662412.name: Calvary Church (PAOC), 9 Capital Drive at Malpeque Road (OSM place_of_worship, unnamed)
400662412._comment: From CBC's photos: From CBC's photo: a windowless block of orange-brown brick (#a65f3c) in stepped sections whose roofs slope up to a tall square-cornered auditorium wall (sawtooth, rising toward the corner), a low flat-roofed brick wing in front, light grey metal coping. 'CALVARY CHURCH / PAOC' in gold letters on the tall brick wall. A pylon sign by the road (dark brown board, gold letters, an LED message screen) on a concrete post with a cross. A tall white cross/pole on the roof. Walls 5 m (wing) to about 11 m (auditorium). The lot is big and open (the site plan the developer had wanted). Pentecostal church (~280 people). Damaged 'catastrophically' by post-tropical storm Fiona (Sept 24, 2022); a plan with BGI Group for two high-rise apartment towers (~400 units), a clinic and a new church on the site was shelved in Sept 2025 when the congregation voted to repair ($3.2M insurance). Roof repaired; inside gutted to steel and block, new offices, cafe, bigger auditorium planned; not reopened as of Sept 2025. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-calvary-church-fiona-damage-not-turning-into-apartments-1.7636152

400664334.name: Small motel on Thompson Drive / Sandstone Road (unnamed 'hotel')
400664334._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): One-storey motel row, white or beige siding, low gable roof, doors to the lot. OSM tags it hotel; 68x15 m, a single row. Could be a second Best Value Inn block or another motel. Joe's photo should correct it.

400664335.name: Canada's Best Value Inn & Suites, Capital Drive (probably this long unnamed 'hotel' footprint) -> proposed 'Canada's Best Guess Inn'
400664335._comment: From CBC's photos: From CBC's photos: one storey, units back to back with doors front and back, walls of beige/grey stucco and siding (#d9d3c4) with white doors and windows, a long overhanging porch roof along the front on posts, a low dark grey gable roof (#5a5c5e), parking up to the doors. A one-storey motel on Capital Drive. Fire on May 31, 2021 (~30 firefighters), damage to a block of 16 units (eight front, eight back) where 24 people were self-isolating for COVID; cause: air conditioning electrical fault; the fire got into the overhang and attic. Pole sign: 'Canadas Best Value Inn & Suites' and a letter board 'ISLAND OWNED FAMILY RUN'. Which OSM footprint it is is my guess (400664335, 119x36 m, labelled hotel, by Capital Drive; 400664334 is the other candidate). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-fire-capital-drive-1.6049461, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-fire-best-value-inn-1.6050267, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-hotel-fire-charlottetown-cause-1.6056419

400662403.name: Econo Lodge, 20 Lower Malpeque Road -> Make-Do Lodge
400662403._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): A two-storey motel/motor inn, outside doors or a short corridor, beige or white vinyl siding (#e2dccd), the chain's yellow-and-blue sign, pitched dark roof. 20 Lower Malpeque Road (hotel listings), north of Capital Drive near the West Royalty Community Centre. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.frommers.com/destinations/charlottetown/hotels/econo-lodge-charlottetown (snippet: 20 Lower Malpeque Rd)

361877150.name: Comfort Inn, 112 Capital Drive -> Comfy Inn
361877150._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): The chain's older two-storey (or three) motor-inn: beige stucco/siding (#d7cbb5) with a blue or terracotta accent band, a gabled entry canopy, a pitched grey roof or flat roof with a mansard skirt. Corridors inside, PTAC grilles under each window. 112 Capital Drive (hotel listings), between Capital Drive and Thompson Drive. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://ca.hotels.com/ho133276/comfort-inn-charlottetown-canada (snippet: 112 Capital Dr)

701204178.name: Hampton Inn & Suites, 300 Capital Drive -> Hamlet Inn
701204178._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess from the chain's current prototype: six storeys, a mix of light grey and white panels (#d9d9d6/#f2f2f0) with a dark charcoal accent bay (#3c3f44) and a vertical stripe of the brand's blue at the lobby end, flat roof, a porte-cochere on dark posts at the lobby. About 20 m. D.P. Murphy Inc.'s six-storey, ~120-room (listings: 124) Hampton on a seven-acre site on Capital Drive east of Maypoint Road; announced Feb 2017, construction 12-16 months, so open about 2018-19 (newer than most of the strip; listed as 'brand new' on the tourism site). The developer backed the Ultramar next door in 2017 as the 'gateway to the city'. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-hotel-charlottetown-1.3963960, https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.4371339

403498114.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites, 200 Capital Drive -> proposed 'Workday Inn Express'
403498114._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): The chain's 2000s Express look: four storeys, walls of beige/cream stucco (#dacfbb) with a darker taupe base and bands (#9a8a75), a porte-cochere over the lobby, the logo panel near the top of a lobby tower, small paired windows with PTAC grilles. Flat roof with a parapet. About 14 m. 200 Capital Drive, south side of Capital Drive between North River Road and Maypoint (a Google map in CBC's 2020 detour story puts '200 Capital Drive' south of Capital Drive opposite Grace Baptist Church, with Tim Hortons, Wash World and Speedy Glass to the east at North River Road). Indoor pool. The road in front was closed Nov 2020 to replace twin stormwater culverts ($1.3M). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-cornwall-road-work-capital-drive-1.5782555

400664337.name: Rodd Royalty Inn, 14 Capital Drive -> proposed 'Regalty Inn'
400664337._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess (no photo): a two-storey 1970s-80s motor-hotel grown in wings round an indoor pool; beige/cream siding or stucco (#d8ccb4) with a dark green trim and fascia (#2f4a3a), a porte-cochere at the lobby, a pitched or mansard-ish shingled roof skirt over a flat top (#4b4b4b). 'Royalty' name over the canopy. Hotel at the corner of Capital Drive and University Avenue (Malpeque Road), part of the Island-owned Rodd chain. Used as a meeting venue (an IRAC public review meeting of ~100 people, July 2026), and in April 2020 the province made a deal for truckers to self-isolate there. The city's 2031 traffic plan widens Capital Drive to four lanes by it. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-truckers-discounted-rooms-april-2020-1.5531839, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-irac-review-public-meetings-9.7260597, https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.5950800

450234767.name: Large commercial building west of COWS on Milky Way (unnamed)
450234767._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Plain white or grey metal-clad warehouse, low-pitched roof, loading doors. 1,997 m2, west of the creamery on Milky Way; probably part of the COWS plant (warehouse/cheese) or the outlet complex. Joe's photo should correct it.

450234762.name: BOOMburger, Milky Way
450234762._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Small one-storey building, probably shingled to match the site; a bright sign. Propose 'KABOOMburger'. Burger stand at the COWS/Factory Shops site (OSM). Joe's photo should correct it.

243921554.name: PEI Factory Shops, Milky Way at Capital Drive
243921554._comment: From CBC's photos: From the edge of CBC's 2016 photo: a long one-storey building of weathered grey cedar shingles (#9c958a) with white trim, a covered boardwalk in front, white storefront windows, gabled dormers/false fronts per shop, grey roof. Looks like a seaside-village strip. A row of outlet/souvenir shops beside COWS at the North River causeway, the 'factory outlets along the Trans-Canada at the North River Causeway near the western entrance to the city' (Fodor's snippet). A 2006 listing had the Paderno cookware factory store here. Tenants now unknown. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.fodors.com/world/north-america/canada/prince-edward-island/charlottetown/things-to-do/shopping (snippet), https://bac-lac.wayback.archive-it.org/web/20061210122337/http://www.visitcharlottetown.com/guide/shopping.cfm (snippet)

450234763.name: COWS Creamery factory and store, Milky Way off Capital Drive -> proposed 'Heifer's Creamery'
450234763._comment: From CBC's photos: From CBC photos: a big white barn, board-and-batten/clapboard siding painted white (#f3f1ea), the gable end facing the lot with a huge round COWS logo board (black ring, yellow, cow) high in the gable, yellow trim on the corners and yellow X-braced barn-style doors (#e8b62c), black-framed shop windows and glass double doors along the base of the gable end, a long light grey standing-seam metal roof (#b8bcbf) with three white square cupolas with small pyramid roofs along the ridge, and a long covered porch on timber posts down the long side with a 'Factory Tours' sign. Two storeys of barn, walls about 6 m, ridge about 13 m. The ice cream maker's factory, cheese cave (Avonlea Clothbound Cheddar) and T-shirt printing plant, with a store and free factory tours, at the North River causeway on Capital Drive (Hwy 1) at the western entrance to the city. Its entrance road was named 'Milky Way' by council in October 2016 after the Maypoint/causeway roundabout went in (a summer student's idea). Wowie, the fibreglass cow from the airport's arrivals hall, was sent back to the creamery store in March 2023 when the airport renovated. CEO said in 2023 that staff got ~10% raises. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/cows-ice-cream-charlottetown-milky-way-1.3806544, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-cow-statue-moving-1.6771933, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-average-wages-1.6825618

34954425.name: Royalty Centre, 40 Enman Crescent
34954425._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a one-storey 1970s-80s plaza-turned-office block, walls of beige/brown brick or stucco (#b9a58a), a dark brown metal fascia band (#4a3a2e) round the top, a few glass entrances with small canopies, signs for tenants by the doors, a tall plain gym bay where the gymnastics academy is (high blank wall). Flat roof, about 5-6 m, the gym part about 8-9 m. A big low building (11,225 m2 footprint) at Raiders Road and Enman Crescent: a former mall now used as a multi-tenant centre. The Island Gymnastics Academy has been there about 20 years (CBC, Oct 2023: 1,500 gymnasts, 200 on a wait list, 'completely full', looking at Stratford's campus); Spinal Cord Injury P.E.I. ran exercise classes there; a Little Free Library of French books was set up there (2017). Not to be confused with Royalty Crossing, the mall on University Avenue. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-island-gymnastics-academy-new-facility-needed-1.6997568, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-little-french-books-library-1.4041649, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/exercise-disabilities-spinal-cord-injury-pei-1.6621509

178071616.name: The Home Depot, Buchanan Drive -> The House Depot
178071616._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): The chain's standard box: walls of light grey/beige concrete panels (#c9c4b8), a broad orange band and the orange square logo board over the main doors (#f96302), the doors in a raised tower/entry section, a lumber/contractor entrance at one end and a fenced garden centre with a canopy at the other. Flat roof, about 9-10 m. Few or no windows. Big-box beside Walmart on Buchanan Drive (OSM; open on holidays at reduced hours per CBC holiday lists, COVID exposure site May 2021). No CBC photo found. Front toward Buchanan Drive (north-northwest). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-victoria-day-may20-open-closed-1.7202561

34954392.name: Walmart Supercentre, 80 Buchanan Drive (SmartCentres Charlottetown) -> BuyMart
34954392._comment: From CBC's photos: The chain's 2000s supercentre look, from CBC's photo: walls of beige/tan stucco panels (#cdb994) over a grey split-block base about 1.2 m (#8f8b85); a tall square blue sign panel (#0f53a3) standing proud of the roofline on the front's left half with 'Walmart' and the yellow spark in white/yellow and 'Supercentre' under it; the entrance vestibule to the right is a big terracotta-orange stucco block (#c8693e) with a curved overhanging cap and a second cornice band, 'Welcome' in white letters across it, glass doors under a dark 'Enter' band, blue steel bollards in front. A dark grey shingled mansard-style accent (#4b4f57) on the far right corner block. Flat roof, about 8-9 m walls, the vestibule and sign panel about 11-12 m. A second entrance (grocery side) usually mirrors it at the other end. Canadian flag on a pole at the far left. The anchor of the SmartCentres power centre (listed at 80 Buchanan Drive). CBC photo from an evacuation in July 2016 (bomb threat; reopened the same day). A 2021 robbery and assault in its lot made the news. Closed on Christmas, Boxing Day, Labour Day and Thanksgiving; 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Canada Day 2026. The front looks north-northwest onto Buchanan Drive and its lot. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-walmart-evacuated-1.3704262, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/charlottetown-police-walmart-assault-1.6001243, https://www.commercialcafe.com/commercial-property/ca/pe/charlottetown/smartcentres-charlottetown/ (snippet: 80 Buchanan Drive)

256746785.name: Apartment block near Kent and Prince (unnamed, 1293 m²)

388739225.name: Perfection Foods, 215 Fitzroy Street
388739225._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Large one/two-storey industrial plant: white or pale beige concrete-block and metal-panel walls, flat roof, loading docks with overhead doors for milk trucks, a few small office windows at the front; stainless tanks/silos possible at the back. Perfectly Fine Foods (Perfection Foods); check which wall has the docks Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/forum-to-be-demolished-1.235943

439503828.name: Purity Dairy (closed; being demolished Nov-Dec 2026), 317 Kent Street
439503828._comment: From CBC's photos: Street front: a one-and-a-half-storey gabled house-like office in grey vinyl clapboard (#8f9aa3) with white trim and a small blue-and-white 'Purity Dairy' sign over the door (blue script); behind it a long low plant: grey vinyl siding, a lower flat-roofed block, a garage/loading door, small dormer; green roofs on some parts. Family dairy opened on Kent Street in Sept 1946; horse-and-wagon delivery until 1958, home delivery until 2007; sold to Amalgamated Dairies (ADL) end of Sept 2023, building empty since. Oct 2026: interior being stripped, demolition expected November or December 2026 because people were getting in and staying there; the family keeps the land, no plans for it. Today (Nov 27 2026) it is probably mid-demolition or gone. best shown as a fenced demolition site with an excavator, or the plain closed building with boarded windows Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-purity-dairy-demolished-this-year-9.7379406, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-adl-purity-dairy-1.6902296

256471129._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Four-storey modern-traditional block: red brick (#8a4535) lower walls with large glazed bays, metal panel accents, a pitched metal roof (dark grey). Guess on the details. $17M, opened for 2011-12, designed to complement the historic campus building; houses paramedicine, architectural technology, bioscience, construction, energy systems, environmental tech, heritage retrofit carpentry, wildlife conservation. Lidar 20.1 m top, 14.2 m eave, gabled. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://hollandcollege.com/News/2011/cast-building-transforming-holland-college.html (search snippet)

Main downtown campus of Holland College (renamed Prince of Wales Campus 2011, after Prince of Wales College). Student association office and High Performance Centre inside the Weymouth Street entrance. A 2009 $40M plan redid the Weymouth entrance and added buildings on the Grafton-Kent-Weymouth-Edward block. Lidar 12.2 m flat, 6597 m² (OSM has it twice: way and relation). Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/holland-college-expansion-to-transform-campus-1.807436, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-community-groups-winter-clothes-donations-9.6970552

405712271._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Plain three-storey walk-up, beige siding, flat roof (guess). The province is turning a six-unit building it owns on Hillsborough Street into an 11-bed transitional housing project, staffed 24 hours with a security camera. Council sent it to consultation in March 2026 and approved it 7-2 on June 9, 2026 after deferring it twice; one councillor voting no cited property values. Which building is not stated; 28 Hillsborough (apartments, flat roof) is a guess. Joe's photo should correct it. 177662576.name: The Sydney Boutique Inn & Suites (the old Notre Dame convent), 55 Weymouth / Sydney Street
177662576._comment: From CBC's photos: Main building: big red-brick block (#8e3f33) four to five storeys (lidar top 22 m, eave 11 m), long rows of tall windows with white wooden frames, a steep dark grey roof; smaller red-brick building beside it with a mansard/gabled roof and white dormers; between them a modern glass-and-dark-frame link with a vertical glass strip. A new black wrought-iron fence with gold fleur-de-lis finials runs round the property along the sidewalk. The Notre Dame convent (Congregation de Notre Dame sisters ran a Catholic girls' school there for over a century; main building ~160 years old). Sold 2014; more than $8M conversion, opened 2017: the big building became 22 apartments (800-1180 sq ft), the smaller one an 18-room 'five-star' boutique hotel; old link replaced by a glass lobby/elevator addition. Project manager: the sisters visit and 'would like to move back in'; whether they can afford it is 'still a question'. Harbour views from the south side. The Convent Inn & Suites Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/convent-notre-dame-hotel-charlottetown-nuns-1.3834799, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/convent-charlottetown-boutique-apartments-1.3463038

r9996322._comment: From CBC's photos: Low and spread out (lidar 8 m): a red-brick one/two-storey street wing (#8e3f33) with a tall white sign board on it, beige/cream siding (#d9ceb3) on the two-storey room wings behind, glassed-in sunroom/pool sections with white frames and bronze glass, gabled grey roofs with gable dormers and a little cupola; covered drop-off porch. A white pylon sign by the street 'Charlottetown Inn & Conference Centre' (blue-grey lettering, a small logo) over a black changeable-letter board. 143-room hotel with 8,000 sq ft of meeting space. Dropped Best Western in Dec 2016 to go independent ('the Charlottetown name is strong enough'); bought July 2017 by a Burnaby, B.C. hotel company. Capital Inn & Conference Centre Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-best-western-1.3892212, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-charlottetown-inn-conference-centre-1.4202732

28331944._comment: From news and listings (no photo): OSM: brown brick, three levels, black roof. A plain 1960s brick block (brown-red brick #7b4a3a), flat roof, rows of windows, glass entrance on Richmond Street. 285024024._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Small grey-shingle shed, gabled. Park maintenance shed. Joe's photo should correct it.

285021530._comment: From CBC's photos: A tiny red board-and-batten hut (#b8312b) with white trim and a dark grey shingle gable roof, a serving hatch with a red-and-white striped awning, black-and-white sign 'THE CHIP SHACK' and 'LOBSTER ROLLS & MORE' on the roof board; menu boards beside the hatch; picnic tables in front. 251166162._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Small one-storey cedar-shingle shop, white trim, a big black-and-white cow-spotted sign. Island ice cream chain's waterfront shop. HEIFERS ice cream (proposed; check no real shop by that name) Joe's photo should correct it.

257483490._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): One/two-storey clapboard, bright painted facade (guess teal or orange), sign over door. Taco restaurant in a small downtown building. Taco Grande Joe's photo should correct it.

258138474._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Two-storey clapboard house, muted colour, gabled. Professional association office in a small house. Joe's photo should correct it.

258138472._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Two-storey clapboard corner house turned restaurant, pale (white or soft yellow) siding, dark trim, gabled roof, patio, big sign on the corner. Well-known lobster/seafood restaurant at the Water and Prince corner, very busy in tourist season. Water King Corner Shop Joe's photo should correct it.

294880436._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): One-storey, shingle or board siding, patio, sign over the door. Small waterfront restaurant near Founders' Hall. Cork & Line Joe's photo should correct it.

251166178.name: Maritime Broadcasting Systems (radio stations), 5 Lower Prince Street
251166178._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Two-and-a-half-storey heritage-style brick or clapboard building, gabled roof; a small antenna mast on the roof; station logos by the door. Radio studios in a waterfront building on Lower Prince Street, beside Founders' Hall. Lidar 13 m gabled. use the game's own radio station names from docs/radio.md on the sign Joe's photo should correct it.

204726361.name: The Roseport (condos), near Water & Hillsborough
204726361._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Four-storey condo with white/pale grey siding and a dark grey hipped roof, white balconies toward the harbour (the cruise-terminal drone photo shows a white 4-storey condo row with balconies behind the terminal; likely this or its neighbour). Four-storey residential, lidar 16 m hipped. Joe's photo should correct it.

204726360.name: Waterfront condominium east of Founders' Hall (unnamed, 3 storeys)
204726360._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Three-storey condo block, red brick lower floors and pale siding above (the Jan 2020 photo across the lot shows 3-storey red-brick buildings with white trim and a white upper section), flat roof, balconies to the harbour. Probably 'the condominium on the water' next to Founders' Hall in the 2020 Hauz story. Lidar 11.3 m flat. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-development-waterfront-1.5416530

204726362.name: Receiver Coffee - The Brass Shop, 178 Water Street
204726362._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Small one-and-a-half-storey heritage railway building, brick (guess red #8e4a36) with a gabled dark roof, big shop windows, café tables outside in summer. The Brass Shop (built 1876) is where the railway's brass fittings were polished; now a coffee shop (Receiver Coffee). Recipient Coffee (Receiver Coffee) Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-vintage-photos-165-years-old-1.5673844

28344744.name: Workers Compensation Board (the old Charlottetown railway station), Weymouth & Water
28344744._comment: From CBC's photos: Two and a half storeys of rough red sandstone (#8a4636) with lighter freestone sills and quoins, a steep grey-slate hipped/mansard-like roof (#5d6266) with gabled dormers and tall sandstone chimneys, and a long low platform canopy (green-grey metal, on brackets) running along the track side and round the corner. Corner of Weymouth and Water. Built 1907 by the railway (E.A. Wallberg), red PEI sandstone with Nova Scotia freestone trim; controversy at the time over the site (residents wanted the foot of Great George), cost overruns and allegations of corruption. Last passenger train 1969, CN left 1983, then a farmers' market, then empty; WCB bought it 1996 and restored it for its offices. add a 3 m deep canopy round the ground floor if the builder can Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-vintage-photos-165-years-old-1.5673844

1269123789.name: Epekwitk Assembly of Councils building (Mi'kmaq Confederacy), Water & Hillsborough
1269123789._comment: From CBC's photos: Three storeys (lidar 15.3 m), dark red-brown brick (#7a3b2e) with a base of rough red sandstone/grey stone, and on the corner a tall rounded glass drum (curtain wall, dark frames) rising the full height, capped by a projecting round flat roof with a warm wood/copper soffit band (#b4703f); a section of charcoal panel cladding (#4a4d50) beside the drum; flat roof. Faces the Water/Hillsborough corner. Built 2019-2020 ($3.6M-5.5M), opened January 2021; owned by Lennox Island and Abegweit First Nations. Mi'kmaq Confederacy of PEI on the 2nd floor, L'nuey on the 3rd, public ground floor for Indigenous art, culture and business (STEAM PEI ran programs there). The rounded corner room upstairs is the Assembly of Councils chamber with harbour views. OSM has it as an untagged footprint (id 1269123789 at the corner; verify). the corner tower is a round glass drum, not a square brick tower Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-mi-kmaq-epekwitk-council-building-charlottetown-1.5838713, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-vintage-photos-165-years-old-1.5673844, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-mikmaq-friendship-centre-1.3893850

251213746.name: Confederation Landing Park bandstand (gazebo)
251213746._comment: From CBC's photos: Octagonal open bandstand on a raised stone platform: white round posts, a grey-shingled hipped/octagonal roof with a small square open lantern/cupola on top, cream-white trim. Wide curved stone steps (amphitheatre seating) step down in front of it to the lawn; an oval brick path loops the lawn. Confederation Landing is the city's waterfront park (opened 1995), events venue for the 2014 150th; Sunday Downtown Farmers Market moved there from Queen Street in 2024 (set up round the park's oval). City revoked a permit for a MAGA-associated musician's concert there in 2025. Holodomor statue installed Sept 23, 2026. really an open pavilion on posts; a prop would serve better than a building Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-queen-street-outdoor-market-moving-confederation-landing-1.7189930, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-memorial-holodomor-statue-remembering-9.7368727, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-sean-feucht-concert-permit-revoked-1.7592026

425993042.name: Peake's Quay Restaurant & Bar (Peakes Quay), foot of Great George Street
425993042._comment: From CBC's photos: Two storeys (lidar 9.3 m), long, with a wraparound second-floor deck under a bright blue awning (#1f5fa8) and glass railings; walls in green-stained cedar shingle (#3f6e5c) with coral-red trim around doors and windows (#d8615a); several steep gabled roof sections with dark grey shingles, gable fronts facing the water, small cupola. Entrance under a little gabled canopy with an oval black board 'Peake's Quay Restaurant & Bar' in white with a boat drawing. On the old Peake's Wharf. Bought by the Dolan family in 1994 (also run the Charlottetown Yacht Club); restaurant & bar and a well-known dance bar. Public washroom on the ground floor costs the city ~$18K/yr to run (council question, June 2020). ~$300K site upgrade 2020-21. Marina has a floating food court (Nimrod's floating pizza bar, Zak's Burgers, The Chip Shack) since 2019 and rental floating cottages. trim is really coral red #d8615a; a deck all round the upper floor Joe's photo should correct it. A large harbour-side deck with teal and yellow patio umbrellas and red chairs, grey wood decking. Gabled grey roof. Seafood restaurant and fish market on the wharf at the foot of Prince Street, seasonal, packed on cruise days (manager adds staff when ships are in, Aug 2025). July 2024: a family of four dined and dashed on a $170 bill; staff posted the security footage to Facebook. Kept a rare calico lobster in the market tank (2017). Stopped automatic straws (2018). Lobster by the Wharf (proposed); honest line idea: 'Market price. The market is a cruise ship.' Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-dine-and-dash-lobster-on-wharf-1.7259779, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-2025-end-of-august-cruise-ships-1.7622282, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-calico-lobster-robyn-crawford-1.4203390

28325937.name: Port Charlottetown cruise terminal building (big unnamed 'retail' footprint by the cruise berth)
28325937._comment: From CBC's photos: A long single-storey shed (lidar 6.8 m) along the wharf: white/very pale walls with a broad teal-green band (#2f8a78) at the base and around the doors, a darker green low-pitched or flat metal roof (#3d6b4f), rows of small windows and roll-up/glass doors. Inside it's open timber-framed like a market hall. Beside it on the wharf apron: a green steel gangway tower (a gantry with a stair and a bridge out to ships). The apron is wide grey concrete with yellow-painted bollards and edge kerb. Port Charlottetown (the harbour authority) runs the cruise terminal; a ~$5M terminal facelift (separate bus/taxi and truck entrances) and a second berth built 2019 so two ships can tie up. Records: 94 ship calls in 2024 (as many as 165,000 passengers scheduled), max four ships in a day; 2026 season opened in April with the Victory I, ~160,000 passengers expected. MSC Meraviglia (biggest ever) called Oct 2019. Sept 2025: three ships arrived in thick fog and woke the downtown with their horns. A 10-ft red-sand sculpture with 'PORT CHARLOTTETOWN' greeted passengers inside the terminal in 2023. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-cruise-ship-season-2026-9.7170452, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-cruise-ships-charlottetown-record-season-1.7118662, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-3-cruise-ships-coming-1.7643448

28331947.name: Founders' Hall (Founders' Food Hall & Market), 6 Prince Street
28331947._comment: From CBC's photos: Two parts. Main hall: red-orange common brick (#8e4a36), two tall storeys (lidar top 9.8 m, eave 7.1), long side with five bays of very tall round-arched green-framed windows (dark green #2f5e4a frames, small panes) in two tiers, a weathered wood panel between tiers; raised tan stone sill/coping, a stepped/pointed gable parapet with cream stone coping over the centre bay carrying a blue-and-white square logo and 'FOUNDERS HALL / SALLE DES FONDATEURS' in cream letters; brick 'X' tie-plate ornaments between windows; short grey roof behind the parapet. Entrance block at the left end: a square flat-roofed tower clad in pink-salmon stucco/panel with a scored grid (#e5b39e), red coping band at top (#a8433a), brick arch panel on its face with a big arched window and 'FOUNDERS HALL / SALLE DES FONDATEURS' letters, green copper-coloured curved canopy (#5d8b7a) over glass double doors; newer signage on it reads 'Founders' Food Hall & Market' in script. A glass curtain-wall link (dark frames) joins tower to hall. Inside: exposed timber trusses, polished concrete, stalls clad in white shiplap and corrugated metal. Built 1908 by E.A. Wallberg as the railway car shop (repaired rail cars). Became Founders' Hall, a Confederation exhibit run by CADC, which closed and sold it in 2017 to the port authority (Port Charlottetown). Port reopened the main floor as Founders' Food Hall & Market in Aug 2019 after delays (20+ vendors: Big Burger, Receiver Coffee, Stir It Up...). Closed March 2020 for COVID, reopened; open 7 days from July 2021. Vax-pass spot-check spat with two vendors, autumn 2021. Since summer 2024 the Downtown Charlottetown Farmers Market (Sundays) sets up nearby at Confederation Landing; its hot-food vendors were told no because the hall already has food businesses. City New Year's Eve party held there. entrance tower at the west end in pink stucco #e5b39e, ~10.5 m, flat with red cap; check which side faces Water Street vs the lawn Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/founders-food-hall-opening-1.5247049, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-founders-hall-1.6091365, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-vintage-photos-165-years-old-1.5673844
