250149933._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess from the style: two-and-a-half-storey Queen Anne house, clapboard and shingle (pale yellow or cream with white trim, dark green or burgundy accents), steep cross gables, a corner turret or bay, wraparound veranda; plainer two-storey annex behind. 1903 Queen Anne Revival mansion built by the Lowe Bros., now an inn with a modern annex; 22 rooms over three floors, pub/dining room; last renovated 2012. Real business: stand-in 'Pownal Arms Inn'. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://tourismpei.com/where-to-stay/dundee-arms-inn (search snippet), https://fodors.fodors.com/world/north-america/canada/prince-edward-island/charlottetown/hotels/reviews/dundee-arms-inn-481946 (search snippet)

28331922.name: Holland College Tourism & Culinary Centre (Culinary Institute of Canada), Sydney Street on the waterfront
28331922._comment: From CBC's photos: Long two/three-storey building in cream-beige stucco/EIFS with white trim, ribbon windows; a white flat entrance canopy with 'TOURISM AND CULINARY CENTRE' in small letters across it over a recessed glass entrance; red-brick accent piers. Big parking lot in front. Harbour side: a glassy dining-room extension looking over the water. On the lawn by the lot: a navy arched sign with a red circle ringed with gold maple leaves: 'The Culinary Institute of Canada', 'HOLLAND COLLEGE / PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND', and a 'Lucy Maud Dining Room' panel below. Home of the Culinary Institute of Canada and Canada's Smartest Kitchen; a six-month, $7.5M renovation (2017) added 8,500 sq ft of kitchens, a marché-style open kitchen area and a harbour-side extension at the back; the Lucy Maud Dining Room (public restaurant) reopened Nov 2017 and again after COVID (2021). Public college: real name fine. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/culinary-institute-canada-charlottetown-renovation-1.4231078, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/culinary-institute-of-canada-reopening-1.4397893, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-dining-room-culinary-institute-of-canada-1.5901577

28331928.name: J. David Stewart Armoury (formerly Queen Charlotte Armoury), Haviland Street at Water and Rochford
28331928._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: mid-20th-century red brick armoury with a tall drill hall (flat or low-arched roof) and a two-storey office/mess front block; flagpoles and maybe a display gun or vehicle on the lawn. Canadian Forces armoury at the corner of Water and Rochford streets (P.E.I. Regiment, 3 Haviland Street); drill floor used for the Battle of Britain ceremony. Renamed from Queen Charlotte Armoury. The regiment marked its 150th anniversary in 2025. A person's name: sign as 'The Armoury' / 'P.E.I. Regiment'. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-battle-of-britain-ceremony-cadets-1.6967263, https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/video/9.6694065, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-99-unit-apartment-building-charlottetown-waterfront-1.5696514

385049596.name: The Haviland Club, 2 Haviland Street
385049596._comment: From CBC's photos: Italianate mansion in white clapboard: two and a half/three storeys, two-storey bay windows with tall round-headed windows, bracketed cornice, low-pitched (hipped) roof, a tall red brick chimney, a small front porch with red-painted steps and a flagpole bracket; big old trees on the lawn. Private club in a grand house built after an 1866 fire by the widow Esther Lowden (cost GBP 4,500 when a modest house cost about 250). Was the Officers' Club (men only), became the Haviland Club in 1997, women admitted 1999; hosts New Year's levees; said to be haunted by three or four spirits; rentable for events. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-open-doors-festival-comes-to-charlottetown-1.5156448, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-levee-day-returns-2023-1.6699527

389591195.name: Kirk of St. James (Presbyterian), 35 Fitzroy Street
389591195._comment: From CBC's photos: Grey-buff freestone Gothic church, steep dark slate roof, pointed windows with red sandstone dressings, buttresses; a square stone tower with a very tall, slender dark octagonal stone/slate spire with small gabled lucarnes round its base, topped by a cross/finial. The spire is the tallest point on the downtown west skyline (visible behind the Rodd in the 2024 drone photo). Cornerstone laid 7 June 1877, dedicated 20 October 1878, Gothic Revival by David Stirling (Halifax) with W.C. Harris; replaced the 1831 kirk. Built of Wallace, Nova Scotia freestone with red Island sandstone doorway facings, buttresses and window surrounds. Tower walls 20 inches thick; the spire reaches about 130 ft (40 m): a tall octagonal spire with gabled lucarnes at the base of each side. Famous for the 1853 'phantom bell ringers' ghost story (Canada Post stamp, 2016) and lobster suppers. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/charlottetown-ghost-stamp-1.3752838, https://peihistory.blogspot.com/2017/01/kirk-of-st-james-charlottetown-pei-self.html (search snippet), https://waymarking.com/waymarks/wm16Y8D_Kirk_of_St_James_Charlottetown_Prince_Edward_island_Canada (search snippet)

389565014.name: St. Peter's Cathedral (Anglican) and All Souls' Chapel, Rochford Square
389565014._comment: From CBC's photos: Cathedral: dark red brick Gothic church, steep dark slate roof, pointed lancet windows, buttresses; (guess) a modest belfry/bellcote rather than a tall spire. All Souls' Chapel: small, very steep gabled chapel in rough red-brown Island sandstone with a big pointed window in the gable end and a red door, set lower and attached to the cathedral. A black sign board on two black posts with gold lettering and the diocesan crest: 'St. Peter's Cathedral / Anglican / All Souls' Chapel'. Anglican cathedral founded 1869, almost entirely brick with little stone trim; All Souls' Chapel (1888, William Critchlow Harris, built by the Lowe Brothers, paintings by Robert Harris) is attached on its west side, a National Historic Site since 1990, built of rough Island sandstone. The Queen worshipped here in 1973. Faces Rochford Square, the green on the site of The Bog, Charlottetown's 19th-century Black neighbourhood. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/charlottetown-pei-all-souls-chapel-heritage-1.3452588, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-rossiter-queen-casket-edinburgh-1.6582426, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Souls%27_Chapel_(Prince_Edward_Island) (search snippet)

255413796.name: Beaconsfield Carriage House
255413796._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): One-and-a-half-storey wooden outbuilding; guess clapboard painted to match the house (yellow or a deep red), white trim, steep gabled grey roof, wide carriage doors. Carriage house behind Beaconsfield, used for events and exhibits by the heritage foundation. Joe's photo should correct it.

255413795.name: Beaconsfield Historic House, Kent Street at West Street
255413795._comment: From CBC's photos: Second Empire house: golden-yellow clapboard with white corner boards and trim, two storeys under a grey slate mansard roof (patterned slates, dormers), a square belvedere/cupola on top with its own little mansard and iron cresting, tall red brick chimneys; a wide one-storey veranda with white posts and fretwork across the front and side. Formal flower beds and lawn in front. Built 1877 for shipbuilder and merchant James Peake, designed by William Critchlow Harris; run by the P.E.I. Museum and Heritage Foundation, the province's flagship historic site; open for tours, lectures, concerts. Restoration of windows, flooring and siding around 2017-19. Stands at the entrance to Victoria Park; walking tours of The Bog start here. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-beaconsfield-upgrades-1.3989784, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-victorian-beaconsfield-christmas-1.6296622, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-beaconsfield-bog-tour-1.7300606

28326032.name: Daniel J. MacDonald Building (Veterans Affairs Canada HQ), 161 Grafton Street
28326032._comment: From CBC's photos: Big 1980s federal block, four/five storeys, in brown-rust brick: upper floors banded with tall narrow vertical slot windows in pairs, a recessed dark-glass ground floor, a maroon-red flat canopy over the 161 Grafton entrance with '161 Grafton' in gold. 'Canada' wordmark and flag on the roof parapet over the Grafton Street corner. Low federal sign on the lawn: 'Veterans Affairs Canada / Daniel J. MacDonald Building' (blue band, white letters). Blue construction hoarding along Grafton during the renovation. Veterans Affairs Canada's national headquarters. Staff moved out in 2020-21; EllisDon won the $98M contract (design NORR), work started March 2023 replacing mechanical, electrical and safety systems, target spring 2026, cost about $100M; a 2025-26 CBC video says it's on the home stretch. VAC staff resisted Ottawa's return-to-office order because the building was still closed. The name is a real person's: sign as 'Veterans Affairs Canada'. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-djm-building-charlottetown-renovation-1.5865163, https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.6752102, https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/video/9.7094265

158560864.name: Jean Canfield Building (federal offices), 191 Great George Street
158560864._comment: From CBC's photos: Long five-storey block: red-brown brick main walls with a pale green glass and green-panel upper section/curtain wall at the entrance end; a flat concrete canopy on tall round concrete columns over the main entrance; flat roof with a large solar array. A low white federal sign on posts at the walk: red flag, 'Jean Canfield Building / Immeuble Jean-Canfield / 191 Great George Street', 'Canada' wordmark. A round concrete planter/fountain base by the entrance. Five-storey federal office building, opened 2009-10, $54M, LEED Gold, designed to use 60% less energy than an average office, big rooftop solar array (and a 2011 story about new heaters taking the shine off its green rating). Service Canada and Veterans Affairs offices; VAC's temporary national HQ while the Daniel J. MacDonald Building is renovated; passport printing being added (2026). 12 March 2026: a transformer caught fire outside, cut the main power, building on generator, Service Canada and VAC closed for over a week. The name is a real person's: sign should read 'Government of Canada' / 'Federal Building'. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-jean-canfield-fire-offices-closed-9.7133445, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/jean-canfield-building-officially-green-1.998052, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/new-heaters-take-shine-off-green-building-1.877397

205271800.name: Queen Square Centre (offices), Queen Street
205271800._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Likely the three/four-storey pale grey-beige stone-panel office building beside The Guild seen in Street View: punched windows, a glass curtain-wall bay, flat roof, ground-floor shops. Office building on the Queen Street block opposite the Confederation Centre, between The Guild and Grafton/Richmond. No coverage found. Joe's photo should correct it.

158551809.name: The Guild (arts centre), Queen Street at Richmond
158551809._comment: From CBC's photos: Three/four-storey front: a full-height glass curtain wall in dark blue-tinted glass with white mullions, framed by polished black granite and grey granite panels; a giant pink letter 'G' painted on the glass with 'THE GUILD' in white under it; a black LED marquee sign with red scrolling text over a white-framed glass entrance. Faces Queen Street (east, across to the Confederation Centre, whose sandstone shows reflected in the glass). Next to it the brick commercial row with arched upper windows continues down the street. Community arts centre in a 1950s former bank building on Queen Street facing the Confederation Centre: small theatre, a downstairs gallery, rented offices. Ownership passed to the non-profit Ars Longa in 2018. Lost more than $337,000 in three years; Charlottetown council gave $25,000 emergency funding (Dec 2023) as it faced 'imminent collapse'; a Friends of The Guild group formed (Jan 2024); board said in Nov 2024 it had 'turned the corner' by renting the space out on a sliding scale instead of producing its own shows. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-guild-arts-theatre-financial-trouble-charlottetown-1.7109490, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-guild-arts-public-accountability-meeting-1.7383193, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-the-guild-funding-1.7056224

205488403.name: Dominion Building (Charlottetown Library Learning Centre), Queen Street
205488403._comment: From CBC's photos: Seven-storey mid-century office block clad in pale beige limestone-look panels; windows grouped in pairs of white-framed casements in a regular grid; flat roof with a penthouse. 'DOMINION' in tall black capitals running vertically down the Queen Street corner pier, 'BUILDING' small under it (and a tenant name at the top corner). Ground floor on Queen Street: the library entrance pavilion, a flat black steel canopy on thin black columns over a glass wall, with steps, ramps and steel railings down to a brick-paver plaza; a big dark grey monolith sign on a concrete plinth: 'Charlottetown Library Learning Centre' in white with a book logo. Interior: white columns, white shelving, yellow chairs visible through the glass. Former federal building/post office across Queen Street from the Confederation Centre. The public library moved into its ground floor (just over 30,000 sq ft) after 57 years in the Confed Centre; opened 18 July 2022, cost close to $16M, delayed by COVID and supply chains. Upper floors are offices. The library's new front on Queen Street has a café, terrace and outdoor performance pads; a second-floor outdoor terrace. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-new-charlottetown-library-to-open-1.6515097, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-new-charlottetown-library-1.4874301, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-downtown-charlottetown-library-update-summer-2020-1.5647250

250149930.name: Telephone exchange (Bell Aliant CHTWPE01), Fitzroy Street
250149930._comment: From CBC's photos: Windowless block whose top storey is clad in green metal panels with pale green glazing stripes (vertical bands of light and dark green), flat roof with rooftop units; a red-and-white steel lattice telecom tower with dish and panel antennas rises from the roof, well above every other building nearby (guess 45-60 m). Telephone exchange behind the fire station; the tall red-and-white lattice tower downtown stands on or by it. Seen in the 2024 drone photo of the Rodd. Bell Aliant has no stand-in: propose 'Bell Alien' or 'Bellow Atlantic' ('we'll call you back'). Joe's photo should correct it.

250006084.name: Charlottetown Fire Department, Station No. 1 (Kent Street)
250006084._comment: From CBC's photos: 1970s-80s station in orange-buff brick with a rounded brick corner pier at the entrance; a white fascia band over the glazed entrance with the department crest and 'FIRE DEPARTMENT' in red letters; flat roof with brown metal hoods/mansard-like fascia panels and solar panels on the roof (drone photo). Apparatus bay doors (guess: three or four red-framed overhead doors with glass rows) facing Kent Street or the side lot. The city's main fire station and headquarters on Kent Street beside the Rodd; all staff firefighters work from Station 1. A third (West Royalty) fire hall: land bought 2017 for $870,000 near Route 2 and Sherwood Road, design started 2019, put on hold 2023, $6M in the 2026 budget but the mayor says it needs about $12M over two years; the 2026 budget had no money for new full-time firefighters, and the union objected. In Feb 2022 the department told Discover Charlottetown its plan for overhead lights strung across Kent Street east of Great George didn't meet fire code. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-kent-street-fire-department-tourism-code-1.6342839, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-no-new-firefighters-in-charlottetown-budget-union-criticism-9.7154623, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-firefighters-fire-hall-city-1.6735140

250006087.name: Rodd Charlottetown hotel, Kent Street at Pownal
250006087._comment: From CBC's photos: Georgian Revival railway hotel, red-orange brick with cream cast-stone trim: a stone belt course over the ground floor, cream panels/swags under the top cornice, a grey-cream stone cornice, an oval bull's-eye window in a carved cream cartouche high on the centre. Five storeys plus a recessed attic storey; flat roof with copper-green urn finials on the corners of the parapet and a brick chimney stack behind. Main front on Kent Street (south): a white one-storey portico of paired Ionic/Tuscan columns (six columns) over the entrance, with the hotel's name on a black board along the frieze in gold letters. A lower one-storey brick wing with a green (sedum) roof steps down beside the portico on the west. White-framed double-hung windows in a regular grid. Car park and lawn on the east side (toward the fire station). Built 1930-31 by Canadian National Railway (one of six CN hotels, four survive); five storeys, 115 rooms; the Queen stayed in 1964. A $10M+ exterior and room renovation began 2023-24 in eight stages over about six years, hotel open throughout: crumbling brick from freeze-thaw and rusting steel beams, the first two truckloads of replacement brick were 'too orange', new windows, insulation, sprinklers, groundwork for geothermal. Heat and power cost about $1,200 a day (2024). The Rodd chain is a real business: needs a stand-in. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-hotel-rodd-historic-renovations-1.7147015

1257517746.name: New townhouse row, north-east East Royalty / Hillsborough Park edge
1257517746._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Two-storey townhouse rows, each unit with its own front door and small porch; vinyl siding alternating in greys, blue-grey and white, some board-and-batten, gabled asphalt roofs in charcoal. OSM ids from 2024: built after the 2020 lidar, so no measured height. Possibly an early piece of the province's Hillsborough Park development (1,100-1,476 units planned in phases on 34 ha, Fathom Studio master plan, 2023-), or a private subdivision. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-hillsborough-park-dev-2023-1.6933455

388117124.name: Apartment block, East Royalty (St Peters Road / bypass area)
388117124._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): Three or four storeys, vinyl siding: brown/taupe on the older ones (Elena Court was brown siding with white trim), white with a black top floor on the newer ones; balconies, flat or low hipped roofs. Unnamed apartments in East Royalty. The 20-unit building at 6 Elena Court (by the bypass and St Peters Road) burned to the ground June 2024 (about 40 tenants out); if one of these is it, it's gone. Ids 1116108051/52 are newer (2023): probably post-2020 builds. older ones: colour #8b7a68, trim white, roof hipped, roof_colour #4a4a4a Joe's photo should correct it. 451913412.name: Burnwave Energy (the district heating plant, run by Enwave), Riverside Drive
451913412._comment: From CBC's photos: Old plant (photos): a cluster of flat-roofed blocks in white and cream-painted concrete and pale metal, one taller (3-4 storey equivalent) boiler block, several thin dark steel stacks (5 or 6, one tall), sloped-roof tipping bays with big dark openings for the garbage trucks on the street side, a beige metal-clad shed with overhead doors at the water end, a big insulated silver duct elbow by the lot. Beside it, a round wood-chip silo ~15 m high, white/grey steel badly rust-streaked, with a blue domed top. Chain-link fence, flat gravel and asphalt yard by the river shore (red sandstone riprap). A sign on the fence: 'Powering Possibility / Future Home of PEI's New Waste-to-Energy Facility' with the blue 'enwave' wordmark. Burns garbage and wood chips since 1983 to heat ~145 buildings downtown incl. the QEH and City Hall. A $180M replacement waste-to-energy plant (Enwave, Canada Infrastructure Bank loan, province and city) is to be built on the same Riverside Drive site, on the shore point across the yard from the old plant; announced Sept 2025, construction from late 2025/early 2026, working 2028, double the capacity, take 90% of the Island's burnable waste. The old plant (42 years old) stays, decommissioned. The project had been 'three years behind schedule and millions over budget' already in 2022. May 2026: Island Waste says the landfill could last 22 more years with it. add 5-6 thin dark stacks (one ~35 m); a separate white-grey rusty silo (tank style, roof dome, dome colour #3f6fb0, no sign) ~11 m wide, 15 m tall west of the plant by the roundabout Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-clean-energy-waste-processing-plant-1.7630328, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-waste-to-energy-facility-charlottetown-replacement-project-1.6505442, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-energy-waste-plant-expansion-schedule-over-budget-1.6433451

r3441284.name: Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Riverside Drive
r3441284._comment: From CBC's photos: A big sprawl of 1980s blocks, mostly 3-5 storeys, clad in white and very light grey metal panels with ribbed metal bands, flat roofs with mechanical penthouses and vents. Main entrance (photo, 2026): a tall glass atrium of 4 storeys framed in white, with a long low white space-frame glass canopy over the drop-off, flagpoles (Canada, PEI) in front, and orange-yellow accent panels on the block corners either side. Emergency entrance (photos 2021, 2023, 2024): a flat white canopy on square white posts across the front of a one-storey grey-metal-panel wing, 'EMERGENCY / URGENCE' in big red capitals on the canopy's white fascia (wrapping onto its side too), a glass vestibule with sliding doors under it, concrete jersey barriers and an ambulance bay beside. Opened April 1982, replacing the old Charlottetown and PEI hospitals; 243-245 acute beds. Main entrance off Riverside Drive upgraded and ER expanded around 2006. Mental Health and Addictions ER opened Feb 2024 inside the same building as the ER (separate space). $1.1M OR/air renovation and >$2M partial roof replacement announced Jan 2021. Declared over capacity repeatedly (Nov 2023, June 2023: all 245 beds full, 15 admitted patients stuck in ER). AI weapons scanner made permanent at the ER doors April 2026 after a 2-week pilot found 30+ weapons. Oct 2026: imaging patients must now register at central admitting by the main entrance first, 30 minutes early. Dec 2025: $1M donation for cafeteria, a 'music corner' and a staff outdoor terrace. Heated by the district heating plant on Riverside Drive. 2026-27 capital budget: $43.2M to upgrade the QEH's building operations. keep lidar heights; accent panels #e39a2a on block corners beside the main entrance; main entrance an atrium entrance {shape: tower, height 16, cap_colour '#f2f2f2'} with glass; ER: a canopy unit with sign Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-health-queen-elizabeth-hospital-admitting-imaging-9.7396840, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-new-mental-health-emergency-department-1.7123896, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-queen-elizabeth-hospital-renovation-1.5869935

362436766._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: one/two-storey brick fire hall with three or four red overhead bay doors facing St Peters Road, a flat roof, a hose tower, 'Station 2' lettering. Station 2, run entirely by volunteers. 2017 the city bought land to replace it; 2019 residents objected, so it stays and a third station goes in West Royalty instead. Third-station design began 2019, paused 2023, $6M budgeted 2026 ('about $12 million over two years'); the mayor said Station 2 'will remain in place, but will require upgrades'. Union wants more full-time firefighters; mayor: 'let's build it, then we'll staff'. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-no-new-firefighters-in-charlottetown-budget-union-criticism-9.7154623, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-1.5204757

July 2019 fire (cigarette in mulch, climbed to a balcony barbecue's propane tank) destroyed the 29-unit, 3-storey building and displaced 52 people, many seniors; demolished Aug 2019. Rebuilt by Killam with a 4th storey (39 units) and sprinklers on the balconies; reopened April 2021 (only 3 of 52 former tenants came back). Footprint match is likely, not certain (nearest big building to Harley Street; the other Harley Street blocks 605896212/214 look the same era). bays in grey-brown shingle #6f6558 Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-harley-apartments-fire-reopens-1.6005417, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-demolition-begins-charlottetown-apartment-building-1.5248118

1303150558.name: Upper Room Food Bank (former Chandler's Home Centre), 15 Plywood Place
1303150558._comment: From CBC's photos: Long warehouse in black vertical metal siding with three white overhead doors and white steel doors, a white-sided office wing with '15' on it, a two-storey part with a band of cedar-toned vertical boards and windows, and a black gabled canopy on cedar posts over glass double doors. Light grey metal roof, low slope. Charlottetown's main food bank moved here from 34 Belmont Street on Nov 4 2024 (about 300 m² bigger, higher ceilings, loading doors); serves ~1,100 families and 950 children a month. Holland College leases the old Belmont Street building. (OSM 389410112 is the neighbouring Plywood Place building; check which footprint is No. 15.) Joe's photo should correct it. 392669269.name: Hennessey Cutcliffe Funeral Home, 33-35 Longworth Avenue
392669269._comment: From news and listings (no photo): A Second Empire house: two storeys, mansard roof with dormers (dark grey/black slate-look), white or pale clapboard, white trim and cornice brackets, a covered entrance porch and porte-cochère; a newer connecting wing to the second house. Lawns and a paved lot. Heritage-designated Second Empire house at 35 Longworth Ave, once Premier Lemuel Cambridge Owen's home; bought by a funeral director in 1963; joined with the Cutcliffe home next door (1978) and the two connected. Own crematorium since 2018. Lidar eave 4.1, ridge 10.4 m. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.historicplaces.ca/en/rep-reg/place-lieu.aspx?id=4012

1563385408.name: Experimental Farm greenhouses (Agriculture Canada), off Allen Street
1563385408._comment: Best guess (no photo or article): A low range of glass greenhouses: white aluminium frames, glazed gabled bays in rows, a white service building along one end. Part of the Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada research farm (35 ha between Belvedere Avenue and Allen Street, est. 1909): research station buildings along University Avenue, test fields, community gardens, ponds (the 'lily pond') and the Confederation Trail. 2002 declared surplus then kept; 2023 Mayor Philip Brown floated housing on it for the federal Housing Accelerator Fund pitch; MP Sean Casey called it the city's 'crown jewel'; Friends of the Farm (100+ members) oppose; the Mi'kmaq want to be consulted and have said they'd like to acquire it. The OSM greenhouse block is 9,157 m², 3.4-6.5 m. ideally a glasshouse look: pale translucent walls, ridged glazed roof Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-experimental-farm-1.7056202, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-tweel-experimental-farm-development-1.7064812

258949130.name: Ravenwood (Experimental Farm house), 15 Crown Drive
258949130._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Two-storey house with a hipped roof (heritage listing), most likely white or pale clapboard with dark trim and a dark shingle roof, central chimneys, set among old trees and lawns on the farm. Federally recognized heritage building ('Building 5' of the Experimental Farm): built about 1820-1828 (granted to Attorney General William Johnstone in 1820); the farm (est. 1909) was planned around it and its directors lived in it. Now offices (Island Nature Trust has been a tenant). Lidar eave 5.7 m, ridge 9.6 m. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://historicplaces.ca/en/rep-reg/place-lieu.aspx?id=10848

28331975._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a mid-1990s federal lab, 2 storeys, buff/tan brick or precast with bands of windows, a long pitched metal roof (dark green or grey), rooftop mechanical units, small greenhouses at the back. A federal 'Canada' wordmark sign on the lawn. Canadian Food Inspection Agency plant-health lab, built 1996, the only plant-health lab in the region: potato, grain, oilseed and soil pathogen testing (PCR, sequencing). Recent federal tenders: chiller/cooling replacement and a greenhouse replacement study. Lidar: eave 5.8 m, long gabled ridge 12.3 m. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://inspection.canada.ca/en/science-and-research/our-laboratories/charlottetown

Entrance canopy with the name. OSM names it The Pearl, apartments, 132 St Peters Road. The 2020 lidar saw only 3.8 m there, so it is newer than 2020 (or was being built). Charlottetown's 2025 official plan made St Peters Road a corridor for taller apartments (6 storeys in the draft; the approved plan allows up to 10 storeys at busy streets). height and look are guesses; Joe's photo should correct Joe's photo should correct it. 362436751.name: Sherwood Business Centre, foot of Brackley Point Road (161 St Peters Road area)
362436751._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess from text and lidar: a one-storey strip/mall of about 8,800 m², pale beige stucco or vinyl over a brick base, a dark shingled mansard skirt along the front over a covered walk, shop glass and signs along the St Peters Road side; inside, a corridor with tiled floor (flea-market photo shows a bright interior). Since Nov 2015 it has hosted a Sunday flea market (about 125 vendors, moved from the North River rink); weekday businesses mean vendors pack up each week. 2025: a unit at 161 St Peters Road (an outdoor/fishing tackle shop, 'Going Fishing') was listed for sale. Lawtons Drugs Sherwood Centre is its pharmacy wing. Lidar: eave 4 m, short gabled parts to 9 m. Joe's photo should correct it. 464565099.name: St. Pius X Roman Catholic Church, 108 St Peters Road
464565099._comment: From news and listings (no photo): Guess: a mid-1950s/60s suburban church: buff or red brick walls, a broad low-pitched gabled roof in dark grey shingles, tall narrow windows down the sides, a plain front gable facing St Peters Road with a glass entry and a modest bell tower or a cross on the gable. Big parking lot. Parish founded 1956 for the growing east side of the cathedral parish; with about 2,300 families it's the largest parish in the diocese; the basement hall is the 'MacKenzie Room'. Hosts large funerals (e.g. former MP George Proud's). No photo found; building style is a guess from the 1950s date and lidar (eave 4.7 m, ridge 9.6 m, short ridge). tower is a guess; drop it if Joe's photo shows none Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-st-peters-cathedral-online-archives-1.5378863, https://www.cbc.ca/amp/1.5332245

605896174.name: Ardgowan National Historic Site (house), 2 Palmers Lane
605896174._comment: From CBC's photos: A rambling 1.5-storey Gothic-cottage: cream/off-white board-and-batten siding, steep cross gables with white bargeboards, bright green louvered shutters, dark burgundy window sashes, bay windows, a long verandah with tan posts and scroll brackets between the wings, dark brown-grey shingle roof, tall cream corbelled chimneys (about four). Set back in lawns and big old trees. Victorian cottage of William Henry Pope (Father of Confederation), who hosted Charlottetown Conference delegates to a luncheon there in 1864. National Historic Site 1966, bought by Parks Canada 1967; the house is Parks Canada offices (not open inside); the grounds and gardens are public. 2019: $304,000 restoration of the 1860s gardens, ~50 of 500+ trees removed, new wooden fences and gates, site hooked to city sewer (was septic). Two Parks Canada EV chargers in the lot. shutters bright green #3f9a4c, sashes burgundy #7a3536; verandah posts tan #c9a77a Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-ardgowan-upgrades-1.4970100, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-ardgowan-restoration-1.5056016, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-electric-vehicles-chargers-parks-canada-installed-1.5767536

28327181.name: Eastblink Centre (the Eastlink Centre) and the racetrack's casino, Kensington Road
28327181._comment: From CBC's photos: Arena: lower walls red-brown brick (split-face block look) with two pale tan bands, upper walls and the big box of the bowl in navy-blue ribbed metal siding (dark green-grey in older photos). White lowercase 'eastlink centre' with 'Charlottetown' below on the navy metal over a loading dock (photo 2026); a red-painted steel portal frame (two red columns, beams sloping up to the wall) over the glass doors of a main entrance, 'WELCOME' banner. Flat/very low roof. Red Shores (photo 2020): a front with a red standing-seam curved canopy on red brick-and-stone piers over the doors, walls of white/light grey panels with big dark-red panels and a gold-red swoosh, 'RED SHORES Racetrack & Casino' sign in red on white over the canopy, ribbon windows, beige ledgestone base; 'TRACKSIDE patio' sign at left. Judges' stand at the track (photo): two-storey white tower with green trim bands and a dark green pyramid roof with a weathervane, bunting on its balcony. Casino had an 8,000 sq ft expansion (new dining/entertainment) from 2025, due early 2026. Opened as the main venue of the 1991 Canada Winter Games; home of the QMJHL Charlottetown Islanders; ~4,000 seats. City owns the rink, province the trade centre half. 2019 city voted to dissolve its board; 2020 Atlantic Lottery looked at buying the trade-centre portion. $54.9M modernization: Ottawa said July 2026 it's ready to fund its share; Nov 25 2026 city agreed to cover interest on an ~$18M loan; construction to start April 2027: more than 5,000 seats, new lobby, reworked front entrance, walking track, new HVAC/ice plant, emergency shelter for 1,000+. Hub of Old Home Week (August) with the fair on Red Shores/Eastlink property. Red Shores Racetrack and Casino (58 Kensington Road, Charlottetown Driving Park, owned by Atlantic Lottery since 2005) is next door; whether OSM's 13,080 m2 footprint includes the casino/grandstand is unclear: no separate casino footprint is in the list. Red Shores block: colour #eceae6, accent #8e1f24, canopy #a3262b; entrance portal colour #c81e2a Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-eastlink-centre-upgrades-9.7270070, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-agrees-cover-interest-eastlink-centre-modernization-loan-9.7435405, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-eastlink-centre-lottery-corporation-1.5421151

1377056538.name: Sherwood Elementary School (new, opened March 2025), Maple Avenue
1377056538._comment: From CBC's photos: Two-storey modern school in blocks: a base of dark charcoal split-face concrete block, upper walls in deep teal-green metal panels, with blocks clad in warm brown woodgrain panels and charcoal metal around a recessed glass entrance; other wings white/cream panels with yellow accent panels. Big window bands, flat roofs with solar panels. Gymnasium is the tallest block (teal over grey block). Built 2022-2025 on the site of the old school; groundbreaking July 18 2022, scheduled June 2024, opened to students March 26 2025 after repeated delays (students got extra spring and summer break days for the move). P.E.I.'s first net-zero-ready, all-electric school: solar panels, geothermal heat pumps, triple-pane glass; 650 students. The province didn't budget a playground; parents set out to raise $500,000 for one. The old red-brick school was to be demolished and its site made a playground. OSM has no lidar height (newer than 2020). East Royalty's new elementary (on the L.M. Montgomery site, done 2028) reuses this design. Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-net-zero-school-open-doors-1.7493580, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-sherwood-school-netzero-1.6524086, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-east-royalty-school-announcement-1.7596791

362436748.name: Sherwood Arena (the Cody Banks Arena)
362436748._comment: From CBC's photos: A long, low barn: white ribbed metal siding on the long sides, a shallow gabled roof in light grey metal, no windows down the sides. The entrance at the gable end has a projecting gabled canopy (charcoal-grey soffit and fascia) on white posts with a slatted white screen, over a wall of tan-and-brown random fieldstone with glass double doors. 'Cody Banks Arena' in white italic letters on the canopy's dark gable. Gravel/asphalt lot in front with orange bollards. City-owned rink, opened about 1966 (about 60 years old in 2026). Home to about 40 minor hockey teams, lacrosse; the Sherwood Lawn Bowling Club is behind it and the small Sherwood Recreation Hall is next to it. Jan 2026: city hired a consultant to plan a replacement 'Sherwood Sport and Recreation Complex'. Apr 16 2026 public meeting showed three options: keep the rink and build a new community centre ($20.4M), demolish and replace both ($53.8M), or a staged build ($57.2M). A condition report found it 'in good structural shape' with parts in poor shape, could last 15-20 years. Decision expected summer 2026; none reported yet. 2015: ammonia leak evacuated the building. Name stays. entrance and fieldstone are on a gable end; check which end faces the parking lot (Maple Avenue side, guess) Joe's photo should correct it. Sources: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-cody-banks-arena-sherwood-sport-and-recreation-complex-9.7167527, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-charlottetown-cody-banks-arena-replacement-9.7068703, https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/ammonia-leak-at-cody-banks-arena-prompts-building-evacuation-1.3143059

28326112.name: Charlatown Farmers' Market (the Charlottetown Farmers' Market), 100 Belvedere Avenue, after the fire
28326112._comment: From CBC's photos (Dec. 2025 to Jan. 2026): green siding under big red metal roofs, a tall false-front gable with the name in gold letters, a lower front section along the lot. A fire on Christmas Day 2025 gutted the front's southwest corner (charred, then covered in blue tarps); heat and smoke went through the rest. The market moved to North River Road in January, paused the rebuild in April (the land is Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada's, and the lease ran out in 1989: it has been month to month since), and said in June it won't come back. The site is built as it stands now: closed, fenced, tarped. Joe's photo should correct the details.

_heritage_comment: heritage_district_m: buildings and streets within this many metres of the origin get the downtown look (Victorian brick blocks and shopfronts, black cast-iron lamp posts). Elsewhere: houses, plain modern boxes for big buildings, and street lights on wooden poles.

brands._comment: World brands: made-up businesses that stand in for real chains, the way the cars do (Hanaka, Toyola, Fjord). Each lists the real chains it replaces, matched by the OSM brand or name of a building, so every location changes at once. Colours echo the real chain's (sign_colour is the board, sign_text the letters) so players know what it is; the names and logos are our own and new ones follow as OSM maps them. 'kind' picks the usual look from brand_kinds; anything set here wins. To rename a brand, change its key (the name on the sign and in notes). Height and roof still come from the lidar. 'posters' lists artwork (textures/ads/, drawn by tools/make_ads.py) put up in the shop's front windows.

Tim Hardly's._comment: Never quite what you ordered. Window posters from tools/make_ads.py (textures/ads/).

Toyola._comment: Our Toyota (Toyota crossed with Corolla): the Corollary, the Pious (a Prius) and the Haulux (an 80s Hilux). Toyota red.

Dodgy._comment: Our Dodge and Chrysler: the Jaunt, the Rammer 1500, the Caravel (a Grand Caravan) and the Charlatan SRT (a Charger). Dodge red.

Nissun._comment: Our Nissan: the Rouge (a Rogue) and the Sylph 240 (a 240SX).

Hyunsung._comment: Our Hyundai: the Ironiq 5 (an Ioniq 5) and the Filly (an 80s Pony).

Kayo._comment: Our Kia: say it fast and it's Kia-o; a kayo is a knockout, which suits the make of the Gadfly GT (a Stinger). Also the Sole (a Soul, a shoebox on wheels).

Suburoo._comment: Our Subaru: suburb plus kangaroo, the Outback make in every suburban driveway. The Hinterland (an Outback) and the Imprezzo WRZ (a WRX STI).

General Motives._comment: Our GMC and Buick (General Motors, with motives): the Yukoner (a Yukon) and the Roadmeister Estate (a Roadmaster wagon). The only GM lot in town is Hillside, built as Chevalet (see landmark 605896236), which sells these too.

Fjord._comment: Our Ford: the Halfton 150 (the game's pickup), the Pony GT, the Crown Vista (a Crown Victoria) and the Bucko (a Bronco). Ford blue, and a lot of trucks.

Chevalet._comment: Our Chevrolet: the gold of the bowtie on a dark board. The Cavalcade (a Cavalier) and the Camarillo IROQ (an 80s Camaro), plus General Motives' Yukoner and Roadmeister, since the real dealer sells GMC and Buick under the same roof.

Countess Auto._comment: Tools, tarps, a 40-piece socket set missing the one you need, and a surplus aisle nobody can explain.

brand_kinds._comment: The usual look for each kind of world brand; a brand's own settings win. Keys are the same as a landmark's (style, colour, roof_colour, trim, shop, awning, sign_colour, sign_text, sign_height, cornice) plus front: parking puts the sign on the side facing the car park, otherwise the street.

gas._comment: pylon: the price sign out by the road beside the canopy (a station's own landmark entry can set its own).

car dealer._comment: showroom: a tall glass showroom out front with a portal in the make's colour, service doors and a pylon by the road ; the lot gets about 18 cars for sale from 'stock' (model ids in scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd, repeat one to stock more of it).

fences._comment: Chain-link fences round mapped areas, by the area's OSM name: height (m), barbed (three strands of barbed wire on top), inset_m (how far inside the mapped edge it runs). Gaps are left where streets and driveways cross. riprap: a bank of armour stone outside the fence where it runs within within_m of the street (height, width).

Irving Oil Charlottetown Marine Terminal._comment: From Joe's photo from the Grafton Street Tim Hortons: a tall chain-link fence round the tank yard along Riverside Drive.

riprap._comment: The yard is banked up on armour stone along Riverside Drive, with the fence along the top. From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive.

Charlottetown Pollution Control Plant._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. Chain-link along Riverside Drive.

University of Prince Edward Island._comment: UPEI: every building on campus without an entry of its own in red brick with cream trim and slate roofs, the way most of it is (CBC's photos).
UPEI: every building on campus without an entry of its own in red brick with cream trim and slate roofs, the way most of it is (CBC's photos).

median_lights._comment: Divided roads that get a row of tall twin-arm street lights down the median, spacing in metres. From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant.

area_styles._comment: Looks for everything inside a named mapped area: buildings (landmark settings given to every building in it that has no entry of its own) and basins (every pond in it becomes a treatment tank with a concrete wall and railing; basin_height, basin_colour).

Charlottetown Pollution Control Plant._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. Low brown-brick buildings behind a chain-link fence, open tanks.

sign_gantries._comment: From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive past the Pollution Control Plant. The green signs over the northbound lanes before the Exhibition Drive roundabout, and the yellow roundabout sign.
sign_gantries.heading: north

highway_power_lines._comment: Highways (which otherwise get no power poles) that have a line of wooden poles and wires along one side: on the outer side of the carriageway heading the given way, offset_m out past its shoulder. From Joe's video driving off the Hillsborough Bridge and up Riverside Drive.

street_power_lines._comment: Town streets with more than the usual single line of poles: both_sides puts a line of wooden poles and wires down each side (the far side's poles carry the street lights there), heavy strings the main road's bundle (three on the crossarm, a neutral, and telephone and cable lines low on the road side), downtown keeps them inside heritage_district_m, where other streets' wires are buried. From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue from the Superstore all the way to Euston Street (2026-11-24): a heavy line along the west side, right at the back of the sidewalk, and another down the east side, the whole way.

curb_parking._comment: Main roads (which otherwise get no parked cars) with a few cars along both curbs, about odds of the spaces taken, on their two-way stretches of at most max_lanes lanes. From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue (2026-11-24): cars parked along the curb here and there from Allen Street down to Euston Street, where it narrows to a lane each way and a turn lane; none on the four-lane stretch to the north.

busy_lots._comment: Parking lots that are never empty: stalls within reach_m of the named street get a parked car in about odds of them, and lots there too small or unmapped for stall rows (store land drawn as asphalt, a drive-through's strip of parking) get rows laid out (seeded by the stall, so the same cars are there every time; cars on a dealer's lot are its stock instead). From Joe's photos driving south on University Avenue (2026-11-24): the plaza, the drive-throughs, the muffler and tire shops and the grocery lots along it are all busy at lunchtime.
